pending_5d_queue.title: A title-only edit silently destroys a task's time-of-day and cannot be undone through the UI
The 'All' chip counts the selected day while its three siblings count globally, so 'All 0' renders beside 'Upcoming 10'

documentation.verdict_basis: One High defect (a title-only edit silently destroys a task's time-of-day and is irreversible through the UI) plus four Medium defects; and two of the nine acceptance criteria cannot be certified as written — the five declared task groups do not exist (only four do) and the calendar's task indicators do not carry task density as the mockups specify. The build matches the DESIGN on the grouping point, so that AC gap is a story-vs-design conflict needing a product decision, not a build defect. Every core mechanism — create, complete, reopen, delete, group, calendar, layout-block integration, per-rep isolation — works.
oracle_gaps: No BL-* invariant exists for task classification (the overdue/today/upcoming/completed predicates and the rule that completion outranks date). This run established those semantics live and they are currently recorded nowhere. Proposed for /qa-review-oracles.
No VC-* bug-catalog entry exists for the Sales Rep or Task domains — a greenfield surface with no historical defect corpus, so the archetype sweep carried no probes in.
VirtoOZ carries no Sales Rep Tasks page, so no {DOC} oracle was available. The two ticket mockups were the only {SPEC}.

visual.methodological_note: axe-core returned ZERO violations on all three scanned states while 11 genuine AA failures were present; nine came from the manual layer and two from Lighthouse. A green axe run on this feature is not evidence of conformance — the Notes label is the illustrative case, because a non-empty but WRONG accessible name satisfies both automated tools.

contract.reason: schema:refresh targets the default /graphql endpoint; this feature lives on the scoped /graphql/sales-rep, which the repo's graphql-schema.md does not cover. Introspected live instead and recorded inline.
established_facts: priority is server-validated against exactly five values (Lowest/Low/Normal/High/Highest), case-insensitive, normalised on store; Urgent/Critical/Medium are rejected
type is NOT server-validated — an arbitrary string persists
name and dueDate are required on create; dueDate is NOT required on update, so update can reach a null-dueDate state that create forbids

updateSalesRepTask is a full replace, not a partial update: omitted fields are nulled and priority resets to Normal. NOT reachable from the UI — the edit form sends all five fields (verified from the captured request body)
an open task returns completed:null, not false; an explicitly reopened one returns false — a tri-state where two values mean 'not done'
isActive is the inverse of completed
an unknown filter or sort token returns HTTP 200 with totalCount 0 and no error — the same silent-empty shape BL-SR-020 already records for this module on other free-form string arguments
server filter semantics: overdue = open AND due < today; upcoming = open AND due >= today (so it INCLUDES today); completed = completed

coverage_triage.detail: tc:scope found no existing case referencing tasks anywhere in regression/suites. Nothing to dispose: no CONFIRMED, no REPAIR, no RE-BASE, no SUPERSEDED. unscannable[]: none. unmatchedObservables[]: 'task', 'calendar', 'due date' — all three matched zero rows, which is the finding, not a scan failure.

test_data.fixture: 14 tasks, group sizes 2 overdue / 3 today / 5 future / 4 completed — all four deliberately different so a mis-wired filter cannot return a plausible number
test_data.decay_warning: Due dates are wall-clock relative. The 'due today' group expires at the next UTC midnight, at which point 2/3/5/4 silently becomes 5/0/5/4. Any suite asserting group membership must re-seed first.
test_data.isolation: per REP ACCOUNT — confirmed live: a second rep reads totalCount 0 and cannot read, update, complete or delete these ids.
test_data.incident: The 3a seeder ran a teardown-and-reseed at ~13:57:36 UTC while the 4a execution lane was already live against the fixture, replacing all 14 rows with new ids. This was an orchestrator scheduling error — the never-parallelise rule forbids it. 4a timestamped the disruption from a partial-fixture chip reading (Overdue 1 / Completed 2 between two readings of 2 / 4) and re-verified every count-, membership- and marker-dependent item at 14:19-14:20 against the restored fixture. B3, B4, B8 and B13 all reproduced identically. No finding in this report rests on a pre-reseed observation alone.
test_data.left_state: RE-SEEDED after the run — fixture restored to 2/3/5/4. AGENT-TEST-TASK Alpha had been left with an EDITED title, a cleared type and a destroyed 07:00 time (the last of which is BUG-1 and is not restorable through the UI at all).
